claims.statement: The bounded TypeScript and Express slice produces deterministic graphs with source-bound evidence.
claims.finding: The declared fixture corpus and local analyzer tests pass for the supported graph slice.

evidence.locator: Fixture corpus, deterministic serialization, and supported construct boundary.
Expected TypeScript/Express graph and evidence contract.
Public supported slice and explicit unsupported boundary.

limitations: This is a bounded construct claim, not completeness for arbitrary TypeScript.

claims.statement: The local workflow compares revisions with evidence-backed semantic diff categories and deterministic reports.
claims.finding: Golden graph-diff and report tests pass, including conservative unresolved and ambiguity behavior.

evidence.locator: Diff evaluation, mutation fixtures, identity, and impact traversal.
Golden semantic diff categories and evidence.

limitations: The report is local and bounded by the documented input, cardinality, and time ceilings.

claims.statement: The read-only GitHub Action provides a fork-safe architecture review boundary.
claims.finding: The checked-in workflow and local security harness enforce read-only permissions, no secrets, pinned actions, and no repository-code execution; hosted Action fixture jobs currently fail before analysis because generated dist/cli.js is absent.

evidence.locator: Fork permissions, artifact boundary, policy modes, and local-only behavior.
Action inputs and report contract.
Local Action fixture and security assertions.

limitations: Hosted matrix execution is not green until the generated CLI artifact path is corrected; local validation is not a hosted pass claim.

claims.statement: The project has a reproducible v0.1 distribution and rollback rehearsal path.
claims.finding: Local package, SBOM, provenance, quickstart, and installed-CLI rehearsals pass, but no public package release series exists.

evidence.locator: Release artifact and local smoke gate.
Package-install and CLI rollback rehearsal.

limitations: A local rehearsal does not establish public release stability, downloads, or downstream compatibility.

claims.statement: Explicitly supported construct fixtures meet the declared precision, recall, and evidence completeness targets.
claims.finding: The local evaluation gate reports the declared supported-slice thresholds and fails on unexpected fixture drift.

evidence.locator: Precision/recall targets and evidence completeness rule.
Curated expected graph records.

limitations: The threshold applies only to explicitly supported fixture families and is not a population-wide accuracy estimate.

claims.statement: Unsupported and unresolved constructs remain explicit diagnostics rather than guessed edges.
claims.finding: Negative fixtures and support-matrix validators preserve explicit unsupported diagnostics with evidence and remediation guidance.

evidence.locator: Unsupported and unresolved behavior policy.
Negative cases, diagnostics, and conservative identity behavior.

limitations: A diagnostic is evidence of an unsupported boundary, not evidence that an equivalent relationship was recovered.

claims.statement: The core analyzer can operate locally without source upload, hidden telemetry, or a required network path.
claims.finding: Threat-model, CLI, Action, and fixture contracts keep source bodies, credentials, background collection, and hosted analysis outside the accepted boundary.

evidence.locator: Threat boundary and accepted residual risks.
M-009 local-first decision and data-flow scope.
Digest-bound privacy/security contract.

limitations: GitHub workflow checkout, dependency installation, and optional artifact upload are control-plane network operations and are separately scoped.

claims.statement: Supported Node, OS, schema, adapter, and deprecation boundaries are documented and validated.
claims.finding: The upgrade policy and compatibility matrix are checked locally, while hosted matrix runs remain affected by the Action artifact and adapter memory ceilings.

evidence.locator: Node support, versioning, migration, and deprecation procedure.
Maintainer ownership and required checks.

limitations: A documented support window does not establish that every hosted runner currently satisfies the resource ceilings.

claims.statement: External repositories have been exercised as a bounded compatibility sample.
claims.finding: The R-005 review records three analyzed repositories and two bounded failures, with no third-party source or graph snapshots retained.

evidence.locator: Five-repository aggregate compatibility matrix.
Revisions, outcomes, diagnostics, and bounded failures.

limitations: The sample is technical and small; it is not representative accuracy, adoption, retention, or product-market evidence.

claims.statement: The repository has defensible traction and recurring user evidence.
claims.finding: No consented external contributor, adopter, retention, release, or usage series is retained; the scorecard explicitly defers traction claims.

evidence.locator: One observed technical dimension and seven not-observed dimensions.
Synthetic maintainer baseline and zero external records.

limitations: Public stars, downloads, issue volume, views, and CI runs are intentionally not converted into traction claims.

claims.statement: Supported line moves, file moves, and refactors preserve architecture identity conservatively.
claims.finding: Curated, seeded, portability, and quality fixtures pass with explicit ambiguity and unsupported outcomes.

evidence.locator: Identity preservation and false-match release thresholds.
Deterministic quality baseline.

limitations: Dynamic or weakly supported renames remain explicit unsupported or ambiguous cases.

claims.statement: Local graph policies support bounded informational and enforcing review modes.
claims.finding: Policy schema, evaluator, composition, exception, and regression validators pass with evidence-linked findings and fail-closed input rules.

evidence.locator: Policy targets, modes, unsupported inputs, and evidence rules.
Zero false-positive, false-negative, explanation, and evidence regressions.

limitations: A valid policy contract does not claim that the policy is correct for every organization or architecture.

claims.statement: Architecture decisions can be linked to graph evidence and checked for lifecycle and drift.
claims.finding: ADR reference, lifecycle, coverage, policy-binding, and drift validators pass on local versioned records.

evidence.locator: ADR reference and reverse-coverage contract.
Accepted local-first strategy decision.

limitations: Lifecycle validation covers repository-authored records; it is not a governance or compliance certification.

claims.statement: External contributors have a versioned adapter contract, starter, support matrix, and review path.
claims.finding: Adapter negotiation, starter, support, lifecycle, isolation, and compatibility fixtures pass locally.

evidence.locator: Adapter API, capability, and isolation contract.
Status, ownership, support, and retirement criteria.
Permission, time, memory, and output fail-closed tests.

limitations: The contract enables contributions but does not establish an external contributor population or supported adapter beyond the declared matrix.

claims.statement: Identity quality has a deterministic release baseline with bounded false-match and ambiguity rates.
claims.finding: The checked-in identity quality digest and thresholds pass across curated, generated, and portability partitions.

evidence.locator: Thresholds, digest, and expiring exception process.
Quality report and baseline assertions.

limitations: The baseline is a curated and seeded local corpus, not an independent benchmark of all refactor styles.

claims.statement: The local policy evaluator retains zero baseline false positives, false negatives, explanation regressions, and evidence regressions.
claims.finding: The policy regression corpus evaluates twice and matches the checked-in zero-regression baseline.

evidence.locator: Positive, negative, and unsupported policy cases.
Deterministic regression and evidence assertions.

limitations: The baseline proves the reviewed corpus, not that every future policy is semantically appropriate.

claims.statement: Untrusted adapter execution is isolated or refused with bounded permissions and resources.
claims.finding: The local adapter isolation harness rejects network, child-process, path escape, malformed, oversized, and non-cooperative adapter behavior.

evidence.locator: Isolated host and fail-closed permission tests.
Isolation and resource contract.

limitations: Isolation is a local process boundary; it does not authorize executing caller repository code or provide a hosted sandbox.

claims.statement: The project has named ownership, review cadence, security disclosure, and dependency-update procedures.
claims.finding: The maintenance contract names one maintainer and procedures, but it explicitly makes no response-time, succession, or release SLA promise.

evidence.locator: Ownership, required checks, dependency, security, and review cadence.
Upgrade and compatibility procedure.

limitations: A named owner and procedure are not evidence of sustainable maintainer capacity or succession.

claims.statement: The adapter and policy surfaces have repeat non-maintainer contributor evidence.
claims.finding: No consented repeat non-maintainer contributor records are retained in the feedback contract or scorecard.

evidence.locator: Feedback eligibility and zero external record boundary.
Synthetic maintainer baseline only.

limitations: The absence of retained records is not evidence that no one used or contributed to the repository.

claims.statement: A bounded Rust adapter pilot maps the declared module, call, literal integration, and evidence slice.
claims.finding: The pilot records 9 true-positive supported edges out of 9 predicted and expected edges, with two dynamic constructs explicit as unsupported diagnostics.

evidence.locator: Rust pilot decision, metrics, and unsupported boundary.
Digest-bound pilot report.

limitations: The metrics do not generalize to Rust constructs outside the named pilot slice.

claims.statement: Broad Rust language expansion is authorized by the Year 3 language gate.
claims.finding: The accepted ADR retains a narrow experimental pilot while broad Rust expansion remains deferred.

evidence.locator: Graduate, narrow, or retire decision.
Accepted experimental Rust decision.

limitations: Deferral is a strategy state, not a claim that broader Rust analysis is impossible.

claims.statement: The Rust pilot establishes accuracy for broad Rust programs and constructs.
claims.finding: No evidence supports this broad claim; only the bounded nine-edge pilot is measured and dynamic cases remain explicit unsupported diagnostics.

evidence.locator: Explicit pilot limitations and unsupported boundary.
Unknown and unsupported semantics remain visible.

limitations: The unsupported status prevents a pilot result from being converted into a broad accuracy claim.

claims.statement: Users can reconcile explicit local runtime observations with static edges without a hosted collector.
claims.finding: The local CLI, bounded schemas, synthetic corpus, redaction, uncertainty, and digest-only reports validate offline; no live collector or production integration is claimed.

evidence.locator: Local input, binding, redaction, and report boundary.
Eight synthetic family-labeled cases.

limitations: Synthetic local cases do not establish production variance, exporter behavior, automatic binding quality, or completeness.

claims.statement: The runtime reconciliation study establishes reproducible behavior under selected local perturbations.
claims.finding: The study records 20 stable replay digests, five classification changes, one missing runtime edge, and one missing-parent record under controlled synthetic perturbations.

evidence.locator: Sampling and uncertainty interpretation.
Digest-only reproducibility study.

limitations: The study does not estimate production variance, semantic correctness, completeness, or absence of unobserved behavior.

claims.statement: The compatibility review demonstrates representative analyzer accuracy across public repositories.
claims.finding: The review demonstrates a reproducible technical sample with three analyzed repositories and two bounded failures, but explicitly rejects representative accuracy or adoption claims.

evidence.locator: Aggregate outcomes, unknown diagnostics, and limitations.
Five reviewed public revisions and bounded failures.

limitations: The sample is not representative of all TypeScript repositories or supported constructs.

claims.statement: The project has a consented public feedback and RFC decision loop.
claims.finding: The feedback contract validates triage taxonomy, anonymization, explicit backlog decisions, consent, and rejection of private telemetry or source payloads.

evidence.locator: Public RFC, triage, consent, and retention boundary.
Synthetic maintainer baseline and explicit decisions.

limitations: A validated feedback protocol is not evidence that external feedback has been received.

claims.statement: The accepted strategy remains OSS-only and local-first without a new trust boundary.
claims.finding: M-009 records assets, actors, data flows, retention, incident response, supply-chain risks, abuse cases, blocking mitigations, and rejected collection with a digest-bound validator.

evidence.locator: Accepted local-first strategy and seven documented gaps.
Strategy ADR binding and hosted-expansion guard.
Versioned review contract and digest.

limitations: A future hosted, team, provider, or broader runtime proposal requires a new public RFC and reviewed ADR.

claims.statement: The project has external adopter feedback and repeat non-maintainer usage evidence.
claims.finding: The current snapshot contains one synthetic maintainer baseline and zero external adopter or contributor records.

evidence.locator: Current anonymized summary and no-traction-claim rule.
Adopter feedback, retention, and contributor dimensions not observed.

limitations: No external record is retained, so the audit cannot infer a zero-user population from the absence of records.

claims.statement: The repository has a public release series with observed stability and downstream compatibility.
claims.finding: No public package release series exists as of the audit; local release and rollback rehearsals are explicitly not a release series.

evidence.locator: Release stability is not observed and no public package release exists.
Local rehearsal boundary and non-release status.

limitations: Negative means the claimed release series is absent at this audit boundary, not that local artifact generation is broken.

claims.statement: Maintainer load, succession, and support capacity are measured well enough to authorize Year 4 investment.
claims.finding: The maintenance contract names one maintainer and a review cadence but retains no maintainer-time or support-load series.

evidence.locator: Named ownership and explicit no-SLA boundary.
Maintainer load and issue quality not observed.

limitations: A single current owner is a governance fact, not evidence of sustainable capacity or succession.

claims.statement: OSS hardening has reduced the project to predictable performance, security, upgrade, and support behavior at scale.
claims.finding: The local pipe covers budgets, property regressions, compatibility, security fixtures, upgrade policy, and documentation; external scale, release stability, and maintainer-load evidence remain unobserved.

evidence.locator: Year 3 Q3 hardening exit gate and Year 4 conditional gate.
Observed technical sample and seven not-observed dimensions.
Maintenance, ownership, and hosted-check replacement policy.

limitations: Passing local quality gates does not establish external scale or a lower maintainer single-point-of-failure risk.

claims.statement: Year 4 hosted, account, source-upload, or hidden-collection expansion is authorized by roadmap completion.
claims.finding: The scorecard, M-009 review, and ADR 0007 explicitly defer hosted expansion; roadmap completion alone is not authorization.

evidence.locator: Decision, alternatives, consequences, and new-RFC guard.
Rejected collection and future review trigger.

limitations: A future strategy change would require fresh evidence, public review, and a separate ADR before implementation.

year4Charter.guard: Year 4 work cannot authorize hosted, account, source-upload, or hidden-collection scope without a new public RFC and reviewed ADR.

entries.title: Keep correctness and resource budgets ahead of scale claims
entries.action: Repair hosted Action artifact assembly, preserve explicit unsupported outcomes, and add representative local scale fixtures before broadening supported claims.
entries.gate: A new scale or language claim requires reproducible positive, negative, ambiguity, resource, and independent comparison evidence.

entries.title: Prefer bounded offline composition over hosted source processing
entries.action: Keep snapshots, traces, policies, and reports local and separately provenance-bound; do not add an exporter or automatic binding path.
entries.gate: Any hosted or account-bearing proposal requires a new public RFC, privacy/security review, cost model, and ADR.

entries.title: Invest in governed local review and maintainer continuity
entries.action: Prioritize ownership, expiry-bound decisions, security response, upgrade rehearsals, and a measured maintainer-load/succession record.
entries.gate: No team-scale governance claim is accepted without named ownership, replayable evidence, and a capacity-backed support decision.

entries.title: Build independent replication and public stewardship evidence
entries.action: Collect only public or consented aggregate evidence for releases, adopters, contributors, independent comparisons, and support load; retain no source bodies or private telemetry.
entries.gate: A strategy refresh must show the denominator, sampling limits, negative results, and reproducible evidence before any traction or market claim.
